#### 1. deficiency of adenosine deaminase 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.472)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5683826)

**Proposed mechanism:** ADA2 (CECR1) (HGNC:2093) —DECREASES→ Adenosine (CHEBI:15324); Adenosine (CHEBI:15324) —DISRUPTS→ Adenosine metabolism (GO:0006170); Adenosine metabolism (GO:0006170) —DECREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —INCREASES→ Inflammation (HP:0011420); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —INCREASES→ Hematological abnormalities (HP:0001870); CSF2RB (HGNC:2496) —DISRUPTS→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); CSF2RB (HGNC:2496) —LEADS_TO→ Severe congenital neutropenia (HP:0001880). Mutations in ADA2 (CECR1) lead to either loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency. In deficiency of adenosine deaminase 2, loss-of-function mutations reduce ADA2 activity, impacting adenosine metabolism and subsequently decreasing JAK-STAT signaling, which can manifest as inflammation and hematological abnormalities. In Polyarteritis nodosa, haploinsufficiency of ADA2 also leads to reduced ADA2 activity, with similar downstream effects on inflammation and hematological parameters. Separately, mutations in CSF2RB disrupt the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, leading to severe congenital neutropenia.

**How to falsify it:** A demonstration that mutations in ADA2 do not affect adenosine metabolism or JAK-STAT signaling in relevant cell types would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, the absence of any inflammatory or hematological phenotypes in individuals with high-frequency variants in ADA2 (e.g., gnomAD allele frequency > 1%) would also weaken the proposed link. _(variant: rs145229119)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ADA2 in regulating inflammatory and hematological processes, particularly its impact on JAK-STAT signaling, could reveal therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both Polyarteritis nodosa and potentially other autoinflammatory conditions related to ADA2 deficiency.
